issues.legal_issue: A jurisdictional objection to revisional interference may be declined when it is raised for the first time at the final appellate stage and the High Court could have exercised supervisory jurisdiction.
material_facts: The appellant argued that the Magistrate acted as a persona designata and that the Sessions Judge and High Court therefore lacked jurisdiction under the revisional provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
The objection had not been raised before the appeal reached the Supreme Court.
The High Court could have treated the matter as one invoking its supervisory jurisdiction under Article 227 of the Constitution if the objection had been raised before it.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to permit the appellant to raise the jurisdictional objection at that stage.
issues.legal_principle: Although a jurisdictional objection not depending on facts may ordinarily be raised at any stage, the Court declined to entertain this one because it had not been raised earlier and the High Court could have considered the matter under Article 227 of the Constitution. The appellant relied on Dargah Committee, Ajmer v State of Rajasthan in support of its contention concerning a Magistrate acting as persona designata and the revisional powers under sections 435 and 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

predicates.appeal_proceeding: The matter is before the court in an appeal.
predicates.objection_first_raised_at_final_appeal: The appellant raises the jurisdictional objection for the first time at the final appellate stage.
predicates.supervisory_review_was_available: The High Court could have considered the challenged order through its supervisory jurisdiction.

issues.definition: When an appellant first raises a jurisdictional objection at the final appellate stage and supervisory review was available, the objection is not entertained at that stage.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory summary procedure for recovering rent does not apply to rent that is claimable only under a lease and is not claimable under the governing Act or its rules.
material_facts: The Board had leased land to the respondent, and the claimed arrears arose from that lease.
The Board applied to a Magistrate for recovery of the rent, and the Magistrate issued warrants for attachment of the respondent's movable property.
The Board's powers to manage and lease property and to fix rent arose under the Act and rules, but the rent liability arose only upon execution of the lease.

The rule that had expressly provided for recovery of rent arrears under the summary procedure had been repealed before the statutory amendment adding rent on land and buildings to the recovery provision.

The Act provided an example of rent claimable by the Board under its provisions where the Board could require an occupier to pay rent otherwise payable to an owner, up to expenses recoverable from that owner.
issues.conclusion: The rent was claimable only under the lease, not under the Act or its rules, so the statutory provision for recovery by application to a Magistrate did not apply. The Board's right to recover the leased rent by a suit under the general law remained unaffected.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 259(1) of the Cantonments Act, rent on land and buildings could be recovered through the specified procedure only when it was claimable by the Board or a Military Estates Officer under the Act or rules; “recoverable” in that context meant “claimable.” Sections 116 and 116-A and the Cantonment Property Rules, 1925, and Cantonment Land Administration Rules, 1937, empowered the Board to manage and lease property, but did not make rent due solely under its lease claimable under the Act or rules. Sections 256 and 257 illustrated rent claimable under the Act. The Court followed Banarsi Das v Cantonment Authority, Ambala Cantonment and held that the general-law right to sue for rent was preserved.

predicates.statutory_summary_recovery_application: A public authority applies to a Magistrate for summary recovery of money claimed as rent.
predicates.rent_arises_only_from_lease: The claimed rent liability arises solely from a lease between the authority and the tenant.
predicates.rent_not_claimable_under_governing_act_o: The governing Act and its rules do not themselves make the claimed rent recoverable by the authority.

issues.definition: If a public authority seeks summary recovery of rent that arises solely from a lease and is not claimable under the governing Act or rules, recovery through the Magistrate procedure is unavailable.
